assessment.nobel_worthiness: Established the physical principles of long-range electron tunneling through proteins: distance and driving-force dependence, the role of the intervening medium, and multistep hopping. This is a quantitative, physics-based account of how redox enzymes and respiratory chains move electrons, and it underlies bioenergetics and biological energy conversion. Original, clear and conceptually foundational.
assessment.attribution: A compact two-person credit that fits the three-laureate limit. Gray and Winkler led the ruthenium-modified protein experiments. Important theory and earlier work by others (Marcus, Hopfield, Beratan, Onuchic, Dutton, Moser) is not in the supplied credit, so priority questions around the electron-transfer theory remain. Marcus is already recognized (1992).
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of independent confirmation and incorporation into textbooks and into the analysis of respiratory and photosynthetic enzymes. Recognition would be timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: How the committee would weigh the contributions of Dutton, Moser and Beratan relative to Gray and Winkler.
Whether the committee sees this as a separate discovery or as a continuation of the Marcus-theory prize.
I have not independently verified details of the experimental priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structures of the Mo-nitrogenase MoFe-protein and FeMo-cofactor, together with kinetic and spectroscopic mechanism work (E4 Janus state, hydride intermediates, N2 binding), address one of the central problems in biological chemistry, namely how N2 is reduced at ambient conditions. This is mechanism made visible in structures and kinetics, which I value highly.
assessment.attribution: Credit is split between structural biology (Rees, Einsle; also Kim/Rees early structures) and biochemistry and spectroscopy (Dean, Seefeldt, Ribbe, Hoffman, who is not listed). A fair three-person prize is hard. I would favor the structural and mechanistic pair plus Seefeldt, but the allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: The structures are very mature. The catalytic mechanism and the identity of the substrate-binding intermediates are still debated, so full recognition may be somewhat early on mechanism but the structural basis is secure.
uncertainties: Unresolved mechanism of N2 reduction at the cofactor.
Allocation among five credited people and unlisted contributors (Hoffman, Burgess, Howard, Kim).
Facts of early structure priority are from memory and not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers allowed structures from micro- and nanocrystals before radiation damage and enabled time-resolved studies of molecular movies of reactions in proteins. It combines my interest in time-resolved methods with structure and clearly opened a new way to see dynamic mechanisms.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the diffraction-before-destruction concept and the first SFX data; Fromme (photosystem I, crystal sample strategies) and Schlichting (time-resolved applications, LCLS and European XFEL) are central. Hajdu's early role is credited as well, and its recognition is limited by his death if applicable. The proposed trio is a reasonable but contested choice. I am unsure of Hajdu's status.
assessment.maturity: Method is established and widely adopted, but the number of biochemically important mechanisms solved so far is still modest relative to synchrotron work. Possibly slightly early.
uncertainties: Whether the scientific yield so far justifies recognition.
Credit among the instrument developers, sample-delivery pioneers and biologists.
Hajdu's status and contribution are not verified by me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is a core concept connecting proton and electron movement in enzymes, water oxidation and molecular electrocatalysis. The theory of concerted PCET and its experimental thermochemical treatment give a unified physical framework for questions I work on directly (cytochrome c oxidase, photosystem II).
assessment.attribution: Mayer (bond-weakening and thermochemical framework), Nocera (model systems and PCET in solar fuels), Hammes-Schiffer (theory) and Meyer (early concept) all contributed. A three-person limit forces a choice that is not obvious. I would be cautious about any assignment.
assessment.maturity: Concept is well established, but the breadth of impact is more diffuse than for a single discovery. Whether the committee will see a single clear discovery is uncertain.
uncertainties: Priority between Meyer, Mayer and Nocera.
A candidacy resting on a line of work rather than a single attributable discovery.
Relative importance of theory versus experiment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing of single biopolymers turned a conceptual idea into a practical single-molecule sequencing technology and a general electrical analytical tool. Importance is high, with clear originality and broad impact across genomics and analytical chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Deamer and Branton proposed the concept and early demonstrations; Kasianowicz showed polynucleotide translocation through alpha-hemolysin; Bayley engineered the pores and chemistry; Akeson demonstrated enzyme-controlled DNA movement that made sequencing feasible. Branton has died. A tripartite choice is contested but plausible.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with commercial sequencers widely used, though the field is more of a technology than a mechanism discovery.
uncertainties: Credit between concept originators and enabling engineers.
Branton's death limits the eligible group.
Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or as biological technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors install precise point mutations without double-strand breaks by combining deaminases with a programmable Cas protein; this is a chemically inventive and highly consequential route to genome editing with clinical use emerging.
assessment.attribution: Liu is clearly the intellectual leader; Komor and Gaudelli were the first authors of the cytosine and adenine base editors. A Liu-only or Liu-with-trainees prize would be unusual. The listed alternate credits (Kondo, Nishida) concern a related deaminase-fusion approach.
assessment.maturity: The first clinical results are emerging, so recognition is arguably early, and the CRISPR prize in 2020 was recently given; this may be viewed as a follow-on.
uncertainties: Follow-on to the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Whether trainee credit would be accepted by the committee.
Clinical durability and safety not yet fully established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy landscape and funnel view of protein folding gave a physical, statistical-mechanical framework for how sequence encodes structure, with Fersht providing experimental phi-value analysis. Physical principles for biological chemistry, of fundamental importance.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes, Onuchic and Bryngelson developed the funnel theory; Dill contributed the hydrophobic-collapse view; Fersht made the experimental connection. Credit is diffuse among at least five people, and the three-person limit is problematic.
assessment.maturity: The framework is mature and accepted, but later AI-based structure prediction (Nobel 2024) changed the context. Timeliness is a question, as the link to a single experimental discovery is weaker.
uncertainties: Diffuse attribution.
Rests on a line of theoretical work rather than a single discovery.
Overlap with the 2024 prize may reduce appetite.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing by synthesis with reversible terminators transformed biology and medicine, with an enormous impact. The chemistry of the reversible terminator and single-molecule/cluster detection is a clear, original invention.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded Solexa chemistry; Mayer (clustering concept) and Rothberg (pyrosequencing, 454) and Ju (terminator chemistry) have claims. A two-person prize is a natural configuration, but there are priority disputes.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and widely confirmed by use. Recognition is more than timely in terms of impact, though the field might be viewed as primarily biological technology.
uncertainties: Disputed priority with Ju, Mayer and Rothberg.
Whether the field is more suitable for Medicine or Chemistry.
